name: Alabama
writtenContract: No specific home-improvement $ threshold found; general Deceptive Trade Practices Act
notes: General work fine under ~$10k, but plumbing/electrical/HVAC are STATE-licensed with NO small-job exemption.

name: Alaska
writtenContract: No $ threshold for written contract; 5-day cancel for in-home solicited sales
notes: Registration required even for smallest jobs; every trade needs Administrator license + Certificate of Fitness.

name: Arizona
unlicensedThreshold: < $1,000 combined labor+materials (no permit; no advertising as licensed)
writtenContract: No broad written-contract $ statute; 3-day cancel for home solicitation > $25
notes: Standout: the $1,000 exemption covers the trades too, so genuine minor like-for-like trade repairs under $1,000 (no permit) are exempt.

name: Arkansas
writtenContract: Home Solicitation Sales Act — 3-day cancel > $25; 'no license, no sue' rule
notes: General work exempt ≤ $2,000, but plumbing/electrical/HVAC need separate STATE specialty licenses at ANY value.

name: California
unlicensedThreshold: < $1,000 (only if no permit AND no employees on the job)
writtenContract: B&P §7159 — written contract > $500; deposit cap = lesser of $1,000 or 10%
notes: $1,000 exemption is real but fragile — voided by any permit or any hired helper. Gate jobs by permit, not just price.

name: Colorado
writtenContract: No statewide home-improvement contract statute; general Consumer Protection Act
notes: Plumbing & electrical state-regulated (DORA); HVAC + GC are a local patchwork — effort scales with # of cities served.

name: Connecticut
writtenContract: CT Home Improvement Act §20-418+ — written contract > $200, 3-day cancel, HIC # required
notes: Registration cheap/easy but the $200 threshold catches nearly every job; trade work needs a separate state trade license.

name: Delaware
writtenContract: Home Improvement Protection Act 6 Del.C. §2571–2577 — written contract above threshold; deposit cap 1/3
notes: No skill-based license for general work (just registration); trade work needs state licenses; mind 1/3 deposit cap.

name: Florida
writtenContract: Fla. Stat. §489.126/.128 — deposit > 10% triggers permit/start duties; no clear written-contract $ threshold
notes: Electrical/plumbing/HVAC are state-licensed with NO minor-repair carve-out — even trivial work needs a licensed pro.

name: Georgia
writtenContract: No prominent statewide home-improvement $ threshold; most cities require occupational-tax license
notes: Non-trade work under $2,500 workable, but plumbing/electrical/conditioned-air AND low-voltage/networking are state-licensed at any value.

name: Hawaii
unlicensedThreshold: < $1,500 total (void if a permit is required)
writtenContract: HRS 444-25.5 — written contract for licensed home improvement; no $ threshold
notes: $1,500 cap collapses whenever a permit is needed; trade repairs still need state-licensed trades.

name: Idaho
writtenContract: No notable home-improvement written-contract statute (verify locally)
notes: The $2,000 exemption does NOT cover plumbing/electrical/HVAC — those need state trade licenses regardless.

name: Illinois
writtenContract: Home Repair & Remodeling Act — written contract over $1,000 (pamphlet over $500)
notes: Plumbing is state-licensed statewide; electrical/HVAC/handyman rules are municipal and vary by city.

name: Indiana
unlicensedThreshold: No state cap; local licensing in some cities
writtenContract: Home Improvement Contracts Act (HICA) IC 24-5-11 — written contract > $150, 3-day cancel
notes: No state handyman license; plumbing is the only STATE-licensed trade; electrical/HVAC local. See detailed Vol. 1 profile.

name: Iowa
writtenContract: Door-to-Door Sales Act (Ch. 555A) — 3-day cancel on home sales ≥ $25
notes: Plumbing/electrical/HVAC need state trade licenses even if minor; networking & appliance plug-in largely exempt.

name: Kansas
unlicensedThreshold: Varies by county (e.g., Sedgwick ~$2,500); no state minimum
writtenContract: Kansas Consumer Protection Act; no notable written-contract $ trigger
notes: No statewide licensing at all — but you must map each county/municipality's trade rules.

name: Kentucky
writtenContract: No notable state written-contract $ threshold
notes: GC-free, but electrical/plumbing/HVAC are state-licensed trades.

name: Louisiana
writtenContract: Home Improvement Contractor rules for $7,500–$75,000 jobs
notes: Statewide LSLBC; even small trade jobs need a licensed plumber/electrician.

name: Maine
unlicensedThreshold: None for GC work (written contract required > $3,000)

hvac.note: Local/none for electric HVAC; state for oil/gas (verify)

writtenContract: Home Construction Contracts Act — written contract mandatory if > $3,000
notes: No GC license, but plumbing/electrical are state-licensed; enforce the $3,000 written-contract rule.

name: Maryland
writtenContract: MD Home Improvement Law — all home-improvement contracts must be written
notes: No minor-repair exception; even a toilet flapper or ceiling fan implicates licensing.

name: Massachusetts
unlicensedThreshold: None for HIC (all home improvement on 1–4 unit owner-occupied)
writtenContract: M.G.L. c.142A — written contract required over $1,000
notes: HIC registration needed even for small jobs; trades separately state-licensed.

name: Michigan
writtenContract: MI Occupational Code requires written residential contracts (verify exact $ trigger)
notes: The $600 cap is low, so most repairs need an M&A license; only limited no-alteration exceptions.

name: Minnesota
unlicensedThreshold: < $15,000 gross annual receipts (with Certificate of Exemption)
writtenContract: MN Ch. 326B + warranty statute 327A; written contract advised
notes: Multi-trade repairs trigger a remodeler license; single-trade or < $15k receipts exempt.

name: Mississippi
writtenContract: Residential Builders Law — licensed builder for contracts over $10,000
notes: Minor like-for-like repairs under $10k largely exempt; watch local trade rules.

name: Missouri
unlicensedThreshold: n/a statewide; depends on city ordinance
writtenContract: None statewide (workers' comp required, RSMo 287)
notes: Among the most permissive — compliance is driven entirely by target-city ordinances.

name: Montana
unlicensedThreshold: none — registration required for most work (verify small-job exemption)
writtenContract: Montana Consumer Protection Act; no specific written-contract $ trigger (verify)
notes: Registration plus state plumbing/electrical licenses make trade repairs harder.

name: Nebraska
writtenContract: None notable statewide (verify); local ordinances govern
notes: Cheap $25 registration; electrical needs a state license, plumbing/HVAC are local.

name: Nevada
unlicensedThreshold: < $1,000 total, no permit, no regulated trade (very narrow)
writtenContract: NRS Ch. 624; written-contract $ threshold — verify
notes: Electrical/plumbing/HVAC repairs need a state license at any dollar amount.

name: New Hampshire
unlicensedThreshold: n/a (no general license); trades still regulated
writtenContract: Consumer Protection Act RSA 358-A; no notable $ threshold
notes: General & HVAC repairs need no state license; only electrical/plumbing require state licensure.

name: New Jersey
writtenContract: Consumer Fraud Act / N.J.A.C. 13:45A-16 — written contract required $500+
notes: Must register as HIC ($500k liability); electrical/plumbing/HVAC need separate state licenses.

name: New Mexico
writtenContract: Construction Industries Licensing Act, NMSA Ch. 60-13; no notable written-contract $ threshold
notes: Small repairs under $7,200 exempt, but regulated-trade work still needs a CID license (verify).

name: New York
unlicensedThreshold: n/a statewide; set by locality (verify each)
writtenContract: GBL Article 36-A — written contract for home improvement over $500
notes: Local HIC licenses cover 'repair' broadly; a minor-repair exemption is unlikely in the big markets.

name: North Carolina

electrical.note: State (NCBEEC; no small-job exemption — tightest trade)

writtenContract: No state written-contract threshold; Statute of Frauds only
notes: Electrical is the compliance risk — even minor repairs need a licensed electrician; plumbing/HVAC have minor-repair carve-outs.

name: North Dakota

plumbing.note: State (ND Plumbing Board); no dollar repair exemption

writtenContract: No specific home-improvement statute; NDCC 51-15 consumer fraud applies
notes: Plumbing/electrical need state licenses regardless of size; HVAC/appliance/networking freer.

name: Ohio
writtenContract: HSSA (ORC 1345.21, > $25, 3-day cancel); HCSSA written contract at $25,000+
notes: Residential minor repairs fall outside OCILB — only local permits/licensing apply (verify per city).

name: Oklahoma
writtenContract: No notable home-improvement statute; general statute of frauds only (verify)
notes: General repairs need no state license, but trade work (electrical/plumbing/HVAC) is state-regulated even when minor.

name: Oregon
unlicensedThreshold: none — any paid construction/repair triggers CCB
writtenContract: No specific written-contract $ trigger identified — verify
notes: Outlier: no small-job exemption — even minor like-for-like repairs require CCB registration.

name: Pennsylvania
writtenContract: HICPA (73 P.S. §517) — written contract required for jobs > $500
notes: Register HIC with the AG if revenue > $5k; written contract mandatory over $500.

name: Rhode Island
writtenContract: Contractors' Registration Act; written contract expected — verify $ trigger
notes: Low $500 trigger catches nearly all jobs; trades separately state-licensed.

name: South Carolina
writtenContract: $5k surety bond for projects > $5,000; SC Unfair Trade Practices Act (verify written-contract rule)
notes: Very low $500 trigger; even minor trade repairs likely need a trade license.

name: South Dakota

hvac.note: Local (no state HVAC license; e.g., Sioux Falls)

writtenContract: No notable statewide home-improvement statute (verify); 2% contractor excise tax
notes: Only electrical/plumbing are gated by the state; HVAC & handyman handled locally.

name: Tennessee

plumbing.note: State (full > $25K; Limited Licensed Plumber tier under)

electrical.note: State (full > $25K; Limited Licensed Electrician tier under)

writtenContract: TN Consumer Protection Act; Home Improvement written-contract rules in named counties
notes: High $25K GC threshold helps, but LLE/LLP licenses are still needed for trade work.

name: Texas

plumbing.note: State (TX State Board of Plumbing Examiners)

writtenContract: Residential Construction Liability Act; homestead work > $5,000 needs written contract for mechanic's lien (verify)
notes: No GC/handyman gate, but electrical/plumbing/HVAC are strictly TDLR-licensed at the state level.

name: Utah
unlicensedThreshold: < $3,000 no filing; $3,000–$7,000 needs DOPL affirmation + insurance
writtenContract: Residential Construction Contracts Act (Title 13 Ch. 50); no $ threshold
notes: The handyman exemption bars electrical/plumbing/HVAC/gas at ANY price — all core trades need state licenses.

name: Vermont

plumbing.note: State (Division of Fire Safety); some owner-occupied exemptions

hvac.note: State (partial) — AC/refrigeration (C3) & gas/oil need ES license

writtenContract: 26 V.S.A. §5509 — written contract when labor + materials exceed $10,000
notes: No handyman/GC license, but electrical/plumbing and AC-refrigeration work are state-licensed.

name: Virginia
writtenContract: 18VAC50-22 — written contract for all licensed contractor work; no separate $ trigger
notes: Repairs over $1,000 need a Class C license PLUS a trade-specific DPOR tradesman license (trade license required at any size).

name: Washington

electrical.note: State (L&I electrician cert + electrical contractor license)

hvac.note: State (electrical portion needs L&I specialty cert + reg)

writtenContract: No notable statewide written-contract $ threshold (verify)
notes: Near-zero de minimis ($500, can't split jobs); electrical & plumbing each need separate state certifications.

name: West Virginia
writtenContract: WV Consumer Credit & Protection Act (Ch. 46A); no notable fixed $ threshold — verify
notes: Low $2,500 threshold plus state trade licensing means most repairs need licensed trades.

name: Wisconsin
unlicensedThreshold: n/a — trigger is 'requires a building permit', not dollars
writtenContract: ATCP 110 Home Improvement Practices — written contract by terms; no $ threshold
notes: Trades are state-licensed and ATCP 110 imposes strict contract/disclosure rules; many cities add local licenses.

name: Wyoming
unlicensedThreshold: none at state level; check each municipality

electrical.note: State (WY Dept. of Fire Prevention & Electrical Safety)

writtenContract: No notable state home-improvement contract statute — verify
notes: Only electrical is state-regulated; plumbing/HVAC & GC vary entirely by city — map target municipalities.
